purpose: Identify conditions, exceptions, provisos, savings, transitional rules and interacting provisions that qualify or alter a property-law proposition before a legal effect is stated.
priority_rules: Apply the legally controlling provision for the identified issue and date.
Do not assume a general rule overrides a specific provision.
Do not assume a later provision applies retrospectively.
Do not treat an exception as applicable unless its factual and legal conditions are satisfied.
Preserve saving and transitional provisions when they protect an earlier legal state or process.
Where two provisions interact and priority cannot be resolved from the available authority, mark OVERRIDE_UNRESOLVED.
common_property_interactions: joint tenancy vs tenancy in common
easement vs boundary or title extent
general rule vs special statutory regime
hard_stops: Never state the primary rule without material qualifying conditions.
Never silently discard an exception because the primary rule appears simpler.
Never infer an exception from sympathy, custom or administrative practice.
Never resolve conflicting provisions without an authority basis.
If a material condition is unknown, the answer cannot be marked fully verified.
